question.text: A screw gauge with a pitch of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0.5 </mn><mi>mm</mi></math> and a circular scale with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn></math> divisions is used to measure the thickness of a thin sheet of aluminium. Before starting the measurement, it is found that when the two jaws of the screw gauge are brought in contact, the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>45</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mrow></msup></math> division coincides with the main scale line and that the zero of the main scale is barely visible. What is the thickness of the sheet if the main scale reading is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.5 </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>25</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mrow></msup></math> division coincides with the main scale line?

solution.text:
LC=0.550=0.01 mm

Zero error =0.50-0.45=-0.05

Thickness =0.5+25×0.01+0.05

=0.50+0.25+0.05

=0.80 mm
